comment: Motor 1 had been replaced before this flight; the log shows a high-current event with MOTOR_DESYNC(m0,m1,m3) and LOW_CELL.

Centered-stick event begins as a sudden yaw-rate disturbance at 11.060 s before voltage sag; motor outputs then rail and detector hits alternate across all motors. This does not isolate ESC channel 1.
Second centered-stick event repeats the sudden yaw-rate onset at 10.655 s before voltage sag; first detector hit is m3, not m0. This weakens the single-channel ESC hypothesis.

Bench ramp: m1/Motor 2 and m3/Motor 4 produced essentially no bidirectional-DShot RPM while m0/Motor 1 and m2/Motor 3 spun normally. FC commanded m1 to 100% as yaw diverged, but it remained at 0 RPM. Receiver stayed valid with no failsafe. Diagnose motors, phase connections, and ESC channels 2/4; this is not a PID-tuning issue. The 13.41 V minimum occurs only in the final 11 ms and should not be treated as sustained battery sag.

Failed takeoff, not a flight. ROOT CAUSE: the 4.2.4 to 2026.6.1 upgrade on 2026-09-05 reinterpreted the stored yaw rate. Rateprofile 0 holds yaw_rc_rate = 172, which was a 1.72x BETAFLIGHT multiplier under 4.2 but is 1720 deg/s of ACTUAL centre sensitivity under 2026.6.1, against roll/pitch at 7 (70 deg/s). All three axes rest at the same one-unit stick offset, but only yaw turns it into a command: roll +1 and pitch +1 give setpoint 0, yaw -1 gives setpoint -3 deg/s (-1/500 x 1720 = -3.44, matching the log exactly). Under 4.2 the same offset gave about -0.69 deg/s. With yaw_deadband = 0 nothing absorbs it and the quad cannot yaw on the ground, so once throttle crosses min_check 1050 the YAW I-term alone integrates from -14 to about -70 in 0.5 s while roll/pitch/P/D/F stay at noise level; at liftoff it dumps into the mixer (motors [617,350,180,681], yaw mixer component 768 at t=4.01 s). Departure at t=4.28 s reaches -475 deg/s, 114.8 A, 24.88 to 19.73 V. The 4 s throttle creep is what gave the integrator time. Fix: set yaw_rc_rate = 7 on rateprofile 0, centre the yaw stick, set yaw_deadband = 2, and punch the throttle. flightModeFlags constant at 8388609 - turtle not active, and ANGLE was not in use (pilot took off with AUX2/3/4 at 1000). LOW_CELL is a consequence of the current spike; median current is 1.4 A. Motor 3 being a Racerstar BR1507 rather than the original XING is a separate open item - the quad flew with it. See docs/troubleshooting/green-hornet-post-upgrade-takeoff-failure.md.

Second identical failed takeoff, same root cause. Stationary ramp to 1226 (23%) over 4.5 s; yaw stick again at -1 for every frame giving a standing -3 deg/s setpoint, yaw I-term 0 below min_check then integrating to about -74. Departure at t=4.54 s reaching 738 deg/s, 105.7 A, 24.70 to 18.76 V. Reproduces log 3 exactly, ruling out a one-off snag or pilot input. See docs/troubleshooting/green-hornet-post-upgrade-takeoff-failure.md.

Test flight after the rate fix (rc_rates 20/20/34, srate 67/67/115 confirmed in the log header). THE RATE FIX DID NOT SOLVE IT. It did work as designed: yaw setpoint dropped from -3 to -1 and yaw I-term stayed at -12 instead of -70, so the yaw windup is gone. The quad flipped anyway, and this time on ROLL. Sequence: 4 s of armed idle with I-term at exactly 0 and clean gyro (unfiltered RMS 2.9/8.5/7.0 deg/s - this is NOT a vibration problem). At t=4.4 s throttle reaches 1126. From t=4.72 a real roll develops (gyro -16, -24, -31, -45, -58 deg/s); the FC pins Motor 2 at the 158 floor for ~25 ms while driving Motor 3 to ~1200, and the roll does not arrest. At t=4.75 it reverses violently, accZ jumps 2040 to 2930, motors swing to opposite rails (Motor 2 to 2047, Motor 3 to 158), 114.9 A peak, 24.84 to 20.82 V. Motors reach both extremes while throttle is only ~19%, which is full attitude authority at low throttle. Leading candidate is now feature AIRMODE, which the dumps show was at 4.2's default of OFF and is at 2026.6.1's default of ON. Four hypotheses have now been disconfirmed by test; the log gives the mechanism but not which changed setting causes it. See docs/troubleshooting/green-hornet-post-upgrade-takeoff-failure.md.

Props-off bench ramp after setting deadband = 2 and yaw_deadband = 2 (airmode already off). The I-term runaway is FIXED: all three sticks now read exactly 0 at rest where log 10 had yaw resting at -1; yaw setpoint 0, yaw I-term peaks at -2 against -160 and still climbing in log 10; pitch I-term -1 against +48; motor spread with sticks centred is 6 to 30 across the ramp to 1486 throttle, against a runaway past 253. The roll excursion to -73 at t=7.2-8.0 s is a real stick input (rcRoll -7 to -10, back to exactly 0) winding up against the clamp - a bench artifact. CAUTION: the Motor 3 comparison taken from this log is INVALID for judging motor health. Props-off runs the motor unloaded, which hides a torque deficit; log 13 with props fitted shows Motor 3 at -14% where this log shows -7.4%. Do not use unloaded data to clear a motor. See docs/troubleshooting/green-hornet-post-upgrade-takeoff-failure.md.

First takeoff attempt with props fitted after the deadband fix. FLIPPED AGAIN, and this log identifies the remaining fault: MOTOR 3 IS DOWN UNDER LOAD. Across 2.4 s of steady props-on idle at matched commands, eRPM is Motor1 402, Motor2 419, Motor3 352, Motor4 408 - Motor 3 is 14.1% below the mean of the other three at command 158-200 and 13.9% at 200-260. The same measurement props-off gives only -7.4%, so the deficit doubles under load: a motor that cannot hold RPM against torque. Thrust goes as RPM squared, so 14% less RPM is roughly 26% less thrust on that corner, which is ample to flip the quad at liftoff. The deadband fix is confirmed holding - I-terms sit at exactly 0 through 2.4 s of idle. At t=2.6 s throttle reaches 1092, by 2.8 s the quad is rotating, and by 3.0 s gyro pitch hits 419 deg/s; 67.7 A peak, 24.51 to 22.74 V. Next: swap the Motor 3 prop with Motor 1 and repeat an idle-only props-on capture to separate prop from motor; then replace the motor. See docs/troubleshooting/green-hornet-post-upgrade-takeoff-failure.md.
